lines.trans: Does it not seem to you that our dining room is old?
It is just as old as you are.
Vitya, well how do you feel today?
Dima, I did not drink last night!
Everything is completely fine with me, see?
Yes, understood, what did you want to talk about?
Lately you have been walking around sad and tired.
You definitely need to get a good rest right now.
Your cooks in the kitchen are managing on their own for now.
So go home calmly and rest.
There is no need, Dima, I work great on my own.
This is not a discussion, this is my direct order!
Alright, I will take only two days.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'it seems', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.text: Лучше я сама ему всё скажу.
examples.trans: It is better if I tell him everything myself.

examples.text: Вика, как ты сама об этом думаешь?
examples.trans: Vika, what do you think about this yourself?

examples.text: Сейчас ваш шеф сам готовить будет!
examples.trans: Right now your chef is going to cook himself!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Что тебе надо? Ничего, работаем.
examples.trans: What do you want? Nothing, we are working.

examples.text: Мы раньше долго работали вместе.
examples.trans: We used to work together for a long time.

examples.text: Мне недавно предложили поработать в России.
examples.trans: I was recently offered work in Russia.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Раньше ты так долго не думал.
examples.trans: Before, you did not take this long to think.

examples.text: Слушай, ты пока не переживай так.
examples.trans: Listen, do not worry like that yet.

examples.text: Так, пусти меня к нему сейчас!
examples.trans: Alright, let me through to him right now!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Мы должны всегда идти только вперёд.
examples.trans: We must always move only forward.

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Он идёт на второй срок.
examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Шеф, давай сначала немного спокойно поговорим.
examples.trans: Chef, let us first talk a little calmly.

examples.text: Правильно, лучше всегда спокойно есть дома.
examples.trans: Right, it is always better to eat calmly at home.

examples.text: Так что иди спокойно домой и отдохни.
examples.trans: So go home calmly and rest.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Правильно, лучше всегда спокойно есть дома.
examples.trans: Right, it is always better to eat calmly at home.

examples.text: Иди домой, Витя, до вечера!
examples.trans: Go home, Vitya, until tonight!

examples.text: Так что иди спокойно домой и отдохни.
examples.trans: So go home calmly and rest.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Нет, что вы, всё просто отлично!
examples.trans: No, not at all, everything is simply great!

examples.text: У меня есть отличный план!
examples.trans: I have a great plan!

examples.text: Не надо, Дима, я отлично работаю сам.
examples.trans: There is no need, Dima, I work great on my own.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это очень смешно, Дмитрий Владимирович.
examples.trans: That is very funny, Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Да, это было давно в армии.
examples.trans: Yes, that was a long time ago in the army.

examples.text: Это мой старый друг из Парижа.
examples.trans: This is my old friend from Paris.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'говор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'matter' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Витя, я вообще-то с тобой разговариваю!
examples.trans: Vitya, I am actually talking to you!

examples.text: Вечером нас с тобой ждёт серьёзный разговор.
examples.trans: Tonight a serious conversation awaits the two of us.

examples.text: Это не разговор, это мой прямой приказ!
examples.trans: This is not a discussion, this is my direct order!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это мой старый друг из Парижа.
examples.trans: This is my old friend from Paris.

examples.text: Шеф, это точно не мой ребёнок!
examples.trans: Chef, this is definitely not my child!

examples.text: Иди домой, Витя, до вечера!
examples.trans: Go home, Vitya, until tonight!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('live').

examples.text: Кто отец? Я тебя прямо спрашиваю!
examples.trans: Who is the father? I am asking you directly!

examples.text: Я куплю тест прямо сейчас!
examples.trans: I will buy a test right now!

examples.text: Это не разговор, это мой прямой приказ!
examples.trans: This is not a discussion, this is my direct order!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это не разговор, это мой прямой приказ!
examples.trans: This is not a discussion, this is my direct order!

examples.text: Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I signed the order myself!

examples.text: Это приказ директора.
examples.trans: This is the director's order.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Это очень смешно, Дмитрий Владимирович.
examples.trans: That is very funny, Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Вот новый заказ для Дмитрия Владимировича.
examples.trans: Here is a new order for Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, шеф сам для вас готовит.
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, the chef is cooking for you himself.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will take', paired with 'брать'.

examples.text: Макс, откуда он здесь взялся?
examples.trans: Max, where did he come from here?

examples.text: Возьмите на работу Галилея.
examples.trans: Go and hire Galileo.

examples.text: Возьми деньги.
examples.trans: Take the money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы должны всегда идти только вперёд.
examples.trans: We must always move only forward.

examples.text: Вокруг сейчас столько хорошего и красивого.
examples.trans: There is so much good and beautiful around right now.

examples.text: Она думает, что только она умеет играть.
examples.trans: She thinks that only she knows how to bluff.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф уже два месяца обещает меню.
examples.trans: The chef has been promising a menu for two months already.

examples.text: Уже два часа дня на улице!
examples.trans: It is already two o'clock in the afternoon outside!

examples.text: Ладно, я возьму только два дня.
examples.trans: Alright, I will take only two days.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'day' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне день начинается одинаково.
examples.trans: In our kitchen the day begins the same way.

examples.text: Любишь ты шутить каждый день.
examples.trans: You love to joke every day.

examples.text: Всё, Макс, теперь ты потерял деньги.
examples.trans: That is it, Max, now you have lost your money.

meanings.en: to rest, to take a break
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дыхать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'rest, relax', paired with 'отдохнуть'.

examples.text: Может, тебе уже пора отдыхать?
examples.trans: Maybe it is already time for you to rest?

examples.text: Отдыхай дома, дорогой шеф!
examples.trans: Rest at home, dear Chef!

examples.text: Вы отдыхайте, а мы сами поедем.
examples.trans: You rest, and we'll go ourselves.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'at home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Правильно, лучше всегда спокойно есть дома.
examples.trans: Right, it is always better to eat calmly at home.

examples.text: Иди домой, Витя, до вечера!
examples.trans: Go home, Vitya, until tonight!

examples.text: Так что иди спокойно домой и отдохни.
examples.trans: So go home calmly and rest.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рогой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('expensive').

examples.text: Ты уже стареешь, дорогой Витя?
examples.trans: Are you getting old already, dear Vitya?

examples.text: Отдыхай дома, дорогой шеф!
examples.trans: Rest at home, dear Chef!

examples.text: Это дорогая одежда.
examples.trans: These are expensive clothes.
